ju-ju: a charm or fetish believed to have magical power
calabash: a dried gourd used as a bowl or container
matchet: a heavy broad knife used for cutting bush
palaver: a dispute, meeting, or lengthy discussion over a matter
piccane: a child, from West African pidgin English
camwood: red wood powder used as dye and body paint
bellows: device for blowing air into a fire, used by blacksmiths
fathom: unit of length equal to six feet
pourer-out: one who pours libations as an offering to spirits
sundown: sunset, the time when the sun goes down
mammie: mother, a familiar or childish term for mother
olden: old-time, belonging to former days or long ago
creepers: climbing plants or vines growing through the forest
stakes: pointed wooden posts driven into the ground
noose: a loop of rope that tightens when pulled
vexed: annoyed, troubled, or irritated by something
whereupon: at which point, immediately after which
currency: money or other items used as a medium of exchange
adjoining: neighbouring, situated next to or touching
compounds: walled enclosures of houses belonging to one family
refuge: a safe place of shelter from danger or enemies
corpse: a dead body, especially of a person
commenced: began or started, a formal word for beginning
sentence: punishment or judgement declared by a court or chief
station: government post or outpost of colonial administration
district: administrative area under the control of a colonial officer
native: local inhabitant, a term used in colonial times
cannibals: people who eat the flesh of other humans
witchcraft: use of magic to harm others, believed to be inherited
custom: traditional practice or established rule of a community
rubber: rubber sap collected from forest vines and sold as produce
dowry: gifts or payment given to a bride's family at marriage
lawful: rightful, permitted by law or custom
adultery: sexual unfaithfulness by a married person
sufficiently: to a degree that is enough for the purpose
noteworthy: deserving attention, remarkable or worth mentioning
infant: a very young baby or small child
fancy: to like or desire something; to take a liking to
planks: long flat pieces of cut wood used for building
consult: seek advice or opinion from someone with knowledge
portion: a share or part of something that is divided out
shell: cowrie shell used as money in local trade
